newsitem.title: WESTERN SAMOA: Man escapes burning at stake in Western Samoa.
newsitem.headline: Man escapes burning at stake in Western Samoa.

text.p: A member of the Mormon church was lucky to escape being burnt at the stake after refusing to obey a banishment order by his village council, police in the Pacific nation of Western Samoa said on Sunday.
Police found Lupe Lio, 33, bound to a stake in the middle of the village of Samalaiulu on Savaii island on Saturday, with kindling placed around him by villagers.
During tense negotiations, police and clergymen from neighbouring villages were able to persuade the Samalaiulu village council not to carry out the burning.

Police Commissioner Galuvao Tanielu said the trouble started when Lio, married with six children, criticised legal moves by the village to halt the construction of a Mormon church there. The church is the fastest growing denomination in Western Samoa.
Orders to banish Lio remained in force, and he had moved for his own safety to live with relatives.
Under a controversial law passed by the ruling Human Rights Protection government, village councils have wide-ranging powers over individuals and families living in their district.
